properties.description: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_reasoning_read_back_keeps_its_words_and_pages.rs, on proof trial rung 2's design. (1) At the default budget every returned claim is whole: `says` equals the stored statement, each step's warrant equals the stored warrant, each premise's name its node's name, and no text is cut (64 cut strings on the old code). (2) Read on with next_offset, the pages return all 66 claims once each, in the order an unbounded read gives, and `remaining` counts down. (3) At flo2.io's 27,267 the `page` block names budget_chars 27267, the claims stay whole and the reply fits; 14 of 66 come back. (4) A one-claim page of the theorem still lists con:ax-integer-arithmetic in rests_on and con:def-prime in stated_foundations; on the old code both were []. Plus three unit tests in crates/reflow2-core/src/reasoning.rs: the page versus the walk, a capped walk naming not_walked, and says plus premise names.
properties.findings: 4 passed in the in_memory program and 3 passed in reflow2-core --lib reasoning::tests, 2026-10-17, branch feat/near-matches-note-and-reasoning-pages. All four failed first on main's code.
properties.name: The reasoning read-back keeps its words and pages (4 MCP tests, 3 core unit tests)
